text:
Anya: Heads-up from Sales: two Pilot customers asked for per-tenant routing controls to route requests to different model variants. Competitor shipped it and Sales called it a "must-have" for Dedicated contracts.

Diego: Do we have a clear cost/latency model for tenant-level routing? There are caching and KV-cache invalidation implications.

Ravi: Basic numbers: worst-case tail latency could increase ~15% if we naively key by tenant. We can mitigate by suffixing caches and using a routing layer that prefers shared buckets.

Clara: Options on the table:
- parity shim (API param + feature flag) — quick, limited guarantees
- full-feature (policy UI, RBAC, audit logs) — robust but months of work
- positioning play (market "lite" offering + roadmap) — buy time, risk perception

Anya: Business side: one of pilots will sign a 12-month Dedicated commit if we unblock within 6w. That is material to quarterly target.

Diego: Engineering assessment: we can ship a guarded shim in ~6 weeks if we scope it to API-only, opt-in per-tenant keying, no UI, and a strict canary rollout. We'll need two engineers full-time and one infra on-call.

Ravi: Launch gating checklist for shim (proposal):
- feature-flagged API param for tenant routing
- canary rollout and kill-switch
- short migration doc + limitations section
- perf benchmark suite showing <12% SLO regression on tail
- e2e fallback test to default route

Clara: Marketing/positioning: label it "Tenant Routing Lite" with clear bullets: opt-in, API-only, staged GA. Include a roadmap card for Full Tenant Controls (UI + policies) for Q3.

Anya: My recommendation: accept the shim for pilots to secure revenue, but require strict guardrails: opt-in, SLA carve-outs for early access, and commit to a public roadmap date for full feature.

Diego: I'll spin up a spike today to validate caching strategy and KV churn. If spike passes, we greenlight the 6-week plan.

eng-deploy-bot: canary deployment created: tenant-routing-lite-canary at 1716000300

Ravi: I'll draft the perf baseline and add the fallback e2e. Clara, can you take the customer-facing one-pager?

Clara: On it. I'll also prepare a one-slide enablement for Sales with recommended messaging and the known limitations.

Anya: Great. Reconvene Fri EOD for go/no-go after Diego's spike. Keep comms tight to Sales so expectations stay aligned. :thumbsup:
